metadata.section: THEORETICAL IMPLICATIONS OF THE INFINITESIMAL GENETICS MODEL
subsections: THEORETICAL IMPLICATIONS OF THE INFINITESIMAL GENETICS MODEL
metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Under the classic infinitesimal genetics model introduced by Fisher (1918), a character is determined by an infinite number of unlinked and nonepistatic loci, each with an infinitesimal effect. It is occasionally assumed that each locus has two alleles and that the effects and frequencies are the same (or very similar) across all loci, although these constraints can be relaxed. Here we examine some of the properties resulting from the various infinitesimal assumptions ([[SEE_TABLE:24.1]]), providing a starting point for evaluating the consequences on the short-term selection response when they fail.
